style: late-90s New York street rap, one heavyset MC who treats his verse like a bebop drum solo turned into words: rhythm played as melody, syllables dragged a hair behind the snare then tumbled out in quick clusters, stacked multisyllable rhymes rolling into each other, unbothered talking cadence, a deliberate beat of silence right before each punchline lands. Vocal: enormous man, low velvet chest baritone, lazy Brooklyn vowels, a short asthmatic wheeze audible on every inhale, dry and right on the mic. Instrumental: 88 BPM, swung dusty breakbeat with a thick knocking kick and a hard flat snare, a melancholy after-midnight Rhodes-and-organ soul-jazz figure sliced into a cold, menacing minor loop, walking acoustic-bass-style bottom end, tape hiss and crackle; between the rules a hoarse sampled crowd-chant voice barks the number; bare, minimal, threatening, no hook
exclude: sung melody, chorus, auto-tune, trap hats, 808 glides, gospel choir, glossy synths, cavernous reverb, thin nasal voice, rapid chopper flow, female voice
lyrics:
[Intro: murmured aside, close to the mic]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[Hoarse sampled chant: One]
[Verse: horn-player phrasing, lag behind the snare, hold a breath before the last word]
Number one: never tell 'em what you printed,
trillions out the back door, keep the ledger tinted.

[Hoarse sampled chant: Two]
Number two: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Hoarse sampled chant: Three]
Number three: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout on tick and they ain't paid at all.

[Outro: drums cut, bare voice over the keys]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.
[End]
title: tec-r2-jazz-phrasing
